blockers.summary: §3.4's replacement sentence for the withdrawn two-control overclaim introduces a new false comparative: 'adipogenesis (+0.218) is exceeded by three DDR sets raw **and by more after adjustment**'. The proliferation adjustment subtracts the SAME per-sample proliferation score from every concept, so it shifts every EMC-vs-comparator delta by one constant (0.1829 on GPL3290) and changes no comparison between concepts at all. After adjustment exactly the same three DDR sets exceed adipogenesis, by exactly the same margins.
blockers.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, §3.4. Artifact: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz']. In `contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma`, control_adipogenesis.delta_a_minus_b = 0.2183 against ATR_CHK1_activity 0.2451, S_phase_E2F 0.3111, DNA_damage_checkpoint 0.2564 (three exceed it, by 0.0268 / 0.0928 / 0.0381). In `contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma_PROLIFERATION_ADJUSTED`, control_adipogenesis.delta_a_minus_b = 0.0353 against 0.0622 / 0.1282 / 0.0735 — still exactly three, by 0.0269 / 0.0929 / 0.0382. Every concept's raw-minus-adjusted difference is 0.1829-0.1830, equal to the mean of proliferation_MYC (0.3284) and proliferation_mitotic (0.0374); the mechanism is in emc_atr_vulnerability.py, which computes `adj_scores[concept][i] = scores[concept][i] - pr[i]` with one `pr` per sample shared by all concepts. Containment, stated so the driver can weigh it: the sentence's conclusion ('the reading rests on ONE control') is correct and is carried by the oxphos row (+0.384 raw, above every DDR concept); only the trailing clause is false. The paper prints '—' in the adjusted column for the control rows, so a reader cannot check it from the table.
blockers.fix: Delete 'and by more after adjustment' — or, better, print the adjusted control values in the table (adipogenesis +0.035, oxphos +0.201, myogenesis -0.037, generic DNA repair -0.005) and say what they show: the adjustment is a uniform shift, so it moves every concept relative to the 0.2 threshold and NO concept relative to another. Oxphos stays above every adjusted DDR concept (+0.201 vs a maximum of +0.128), which is the strongest form of the point the sentence is making.

blockers.summary: The fourth of the four part-D bars is called 'fixed before the numbers' (SS5, line 623) and the four tests 'pre-registered' (headline line 99; SS5 line 618), but the producing module's own comment records that this bar was written BECAUSE of a prior run's numbers - and quotes the very numbers the paper still prints. The multiplier chosen with those values visible is what decides the headline count '1 of 4'.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py at the pin, lines 2918-2924, verbatim: '# THE SECOND SPECIFICITY AXIS, and the one the fixed grading actually turns on. / # `atri_specific` above only asks "is this predictor about ATR INHIBITORS rather than about / # drugs in general". It does NOT ask "is this predictor about the MECHANISM rather than about / # PROLIFERATION" - and on run 30857647907 that gap mattered: replication-stress expression / # correlated with ATRi sensitivity at rho -0.164 while the plain proliferation control / # correlated at -0.171, i.e. very slightly MORE.' The bar it introduces is line 2935: `srec["beats_the_proliferation_control"] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)`. Those two numbers are exactly what SS5 reports today (artifact specificity block: expr::replication_stress mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors -0.1637; expr::proliferation_MYC -0.1711). LOAD-BEARING: 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.19677, and the one passing row (dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1, mean rho +0.2123) clears it by 0.0155; any multiplier >= 1.25 makes the pass fail and the count '0 of 4'. SS1's separate defence - 'None of the three has been changed since it was written, which is checkable in the module's git history' - is TRUE (I verified `len(ctrl_up) <= 1`, the `> 0.2` elevated cut and `DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5` byte-identical at d4c623634, 19cc109c6, f45d966df, 1b5f85385, dc8621870, ad87aa4c7, 11d5de12d and the pin) but cannot carry SS5's weight: the module's FIRST commit (d4c623634, 2026-08-05) already contains this comment and four others citing runs 30856488704 / 30857647907 / 30858567419 / 30859156946 / 30859974432, so the history holds no pre-numbers version of the file and 'unchanged since written' does not imply 'written before the numbers'.
blockers.fix: Stop calling all four bars pre-registered. Say which three were fixed before the numbers (direction, |rho| >= 0.15, non-DDR drug specificity) and state plainly that the fourth - beat the proliferation control by 1.15x - was added after run 30857647907 showed replication-stress at rho -0.164 against a proliferation control at -0.171, citing the module comment. Add that the 1.15 multiplier was therefore chosen with those values visible, that its effect on the failing row is conservative, and that the one passing test clears it by 0.0155. Change 'Of four pre-registered mechanism tests, one passes' (line 99) and '1 of 4 pre-registered tests passes' (line 618) accordingly, and drop the SS1 sentence that offers the git history as verification of 'fixed before the numbers' - it verifies 'unchanged since first commit' and nothing more.

blockers.summary: SS3.4 and SS6.1 give irreconcilable accounts of what part B bounds. SS3.4 says the two nulls are 'consistency between two underpowered reads, not a demonstration that a DDR signal is absent'; SS6.1 says 'What part B bounds is real and is the whole of it: EMC tumours carry no proliferation-independent DDR signature, on two series.' A reader cannot act on both, and the arithmetic that settles it is one division of numbers the artifact already carries - the same MDE SS3.4 says was never computed.
blockers.evidence: Paper lines 538-540 against line 782. emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform[*].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma_PROLIFERATION_ADJUSTED carries delta, t and df per concept, so SE = |delta|/|t| and MDE(80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05) = (t_.975 + t_.80) * SE. On the proliferation-adjusted contrast - the one the verdict rests on, since `ddr_concepts_elevated_after_proliferation_adjustment` is [] - every DDR concept on BOTH series is powered against the paper's own 0.2 'elevated' cut. GSE4303-GPL3290 (10 EMC vs 6): DNA_damage_checkpoint {"t": 2.378, "df": 12.7, "delta_a_minus_b": 0.0735} -> SE 0.0309, 95% CI +/-0.067, MDE 0.094; S_phase_E2F {"t": 3.602, "delta_a_minus_b": 0.1282} -> SE 0.0356, MDE 0.110; ATM_signalling_DSB_repair {"t": -1.574, "delta_a_minus_b": -0.0701} -> SE 0.0445, MDE 0.135; replication_stress MDE 0.144; stalled_fork_response MDE 0.153; ATR_CHK1_activity MDE 0.186. GSE24369-GPL6244 (6 EMC vs 29): MDE 0.045-0.118 on all six. Every value is below 0.2. (On the RAW contrast three concepts sit marginally above: ATR_CHK1 0.212, stalled fork 0.232, S-phase 0.212 - but the raw contrast is not what the null rests on.) So 'underpowered' is asserted against no criterion and is false against the criterion the paper itself uses.
blockers.fix: Compute the MDE once and make both sections say the same thing. Replace SS3.4's sentence with the quantified version - e.g. 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours. Against the fixed 0.2 cut the proliferation-adjusted read has >=80% power on every DDR concept on both series (minimum detectable effect 0.045-0.186 in within-sample SD units, derived as SE = |delta|/|t| from the committed contrast blocks); effects below about 0.1 SD units are not excluded, and on the RAW contrast three concepts are marginal at 0.21-0.23.' Then let SS6.1's bound stand with that effect-size qualifier attached ('no proliferation-independent DDR concept exceeds 0.2, with 80% power to have seen one'), rather than as an unqualified claim of absence.

p1s.summary: SS3.2's route table reports 'GEO's curated .annot for these platforms | HTTP 404' where the antecedent is 'the seven platforms' of GSE4303. The committed artifact records no .annot attempt for any of the seven; the only .annot 404s in it belong to three different platforms in three other series. The claim's real support is a source comment about a run whose log nothing in the repository reads.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript line 420. In research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json, `probe_mapping_diagnostic.attempts` for each of GSE4303-GPL2937/2938/3254/3288/3289/3290/3335 is a single entry, the acc.cgi fetch - no .annot URL and no 404. The three `HTTP Error 404: Not Found` records in the artifact are at per_platform.GSE28866(GPL10999).attempts[0], GSE43632(GPL11054).attempts[1] and GSE80126(GPL16791).attempts[0]. The mechanism is in research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 1461-1473: acc.cgi is tried first and the loop stops once a table with an accession column is found, so .annot is never reached for the seven. The row's only support is the source comment on line 1472, 'on run 30856488704 the .annot.gz probe 404'd for every platform' - a run log, not a committed field.
p1s.fix: Either scope the row to the platforms whose 404 the artifact actually carries (GPL10999 / GPL11054 / GPL16791), or cite the module comment and run id explicitly so a reader knows the observation is not re-derivable from the artifact. As written, a re-derivation from emc-atr-vulnerability.json cannot reproduce it and nothing goes red if it stops being true.

p1s.summary: SS3.2a bullet 1 says 'The committed artifact records `ncbi_aborted: "too many errors after 4500 accessions"` with `ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene: 0`'. The artifact at the pin records neither field anywhere; both belong to commit 12e44660c, which only the Appendix names.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript lines 431-433. `grep -c ncbi_aborted` over research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json at the pin returns 0, and no per-platform diagnostic carries `ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene: 0`. `git show 12e44660c:research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json` does carry `ncbi_aborted": "too many errors after 4500 accessions"`, and the Appendix attributes it to that commit. The prose in SS3.2a is present-tense and unqualified, so the pointer is stale in the live text while correct in the Appendix.
p1s.fix: Add the commit id to SS3.2a's sentence, as the Appendix row already does: 'the artifact as committed at 12e44660c recorded ...'. Nothing currently keeps the two in step.

p1s.summary: Almost no sentence in this document is read by any instrument, and a committed measurement says so. Nothing checks the class of statement both blockers above belong to - 'source X says Y'.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json -> papers['research/manuscripts/dependency/emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md'] = {sentences 161, covered 2, with_a_number 123, with_a_number_covered 2, uncovered 159, uncovered_with_a_number 121}. Coverage by instrument, checked at the pin: lint_claims.py DOES read it (via _publication_documents() over systems/graph/publications.json, whose PUB-ATR row's document.file names it) but only grades claim STRENGTH, R1-R5. lint_citations.py DOES read it (it scans every tracked .md) but its test is only that an identifier also appears in some tracked .json/.jsonl - its own docstring calls this 'a weaker and more honest test than is this citation real'. lint_consistency.py lists the file at pinned-figures.json -> targets[18], but of that registry's 99 artifact_figures, 81 superseded, 1 derivations, 1 table_completeness and 1 subset_checks entries, ZERO reference emc-atr-vulnerability - so not one of this paper's ~123 numeric sentences is pinned. No test under research/modalities/tests or research/manuscripts/tests opens the manuscript; the only .py files naming it are lint_readability.py, single_slot_identity.py and atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py, all in comments or as a declared-by pointer.
p1s.fix: Register this paper's load-bearing figures in pinned-figures.json artifact_figures against emc-atr-vulnerability.json and atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json (the grading tier, the four part-D rho values and their bars, the two part-B probe/mapping counts, the part-C group sizes, the section 8.3 TPM/family-fraction rows), so a hand-typed drift reddens the commit loop. Separately, the 'source X says Y' class needs a guard of its own: the two blockers here are both quotations about a source that no instrument can see.

p1s.summary: lint_citations' anchor scan counts blind-review-seat records and hardening-state files as fetch products, which lets a manuscript identifier be anchored by an agent that merely quoted the manuscript.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py -> survey() scans every tracked .json/.jsonl except three named files (citation-provenance-ledger.json, SWEEP_ARTIFACT_REL, TYPE_CACHE_REL). research/autonomy/review-seats/*.json and research/autonomy/hardening-state/*.json are not excluded. Measured at the pin for this paper's identifiers: PMID 34413129 anchors in 8 json files of which 4 are review-seat/hardening-state records; PMID 41651400 anchors in 8 of which 5 are, leaving only research/literature/carfilzomib-class-clinical-2026-08-28.json, research/manuscripts/emc-systems-map.json (a hand-edited registry) and research/method-watch-triggers.json - the module that actually fetched it, atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json, stores it as a bare '"pmid": "41651400"' key, which this linter's own comment states anchors NOTHING. This is the self-anchoring class the three named exclusions already exist for: a seat record is prose written by a reviewing agent quoting the paper under review.
p1s.fix: Add research/autonomy/review-seats/ and research/autonomy/hardening-state/ to the survey() exclusion set, with a test pinning the property (an identifier appearing only in prose plus a seat record must still count as unanchored). Note the exclusion order constraint already documented above TYPE_CACHE_REL.

p1s.summary: Section 8's declared producer still cites the superseded preprint alone in a field a reader sees, which is the exact defect the appendix records as fixed for the other module. Nothing checks that the two producers agree.
p1s.evidence: The manuscript's section 8 banner declares atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py -> atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json as its producer, and the appendix's mechanism-paper row records that emc_atr_vulnerability.py 'went on citing the preprint alone in its docstring and _hypothesis_source' and now names the version of record - true, at emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 10-11, 868 and 3131-3132. But research/modalities/atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py line 7-8 still reads 'The EMC ATR route ... rests on ONE published mechanism (PMID 37205599)', and line ~1070 writes 'Route 1 rests on PMID 37205599, which nominates FET-fusion-driven ATM SUPPRESSION as the lesion' into atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> q3_selection_biomarker._why_this_matters. The module does carry both identifiers as constants (MECHANISM_PMID = '41811428', MECHANISM_PREPRINT_PMID = '37205599') and does ask for the version of record first, so the paper's positive claims about it are accurate; the two prose fields were simply not swept.
p1s.fix: Name the version of record first in atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py's docstring and in the _why_this_matters string, regenerate atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json, and add a test that every module-authored citation of the mechanism paper names PMID 41811428 before PMID 37205599 - a one-of-a-pair guard, since this pair has now been corrected in one half twice.

p1s.summary: The FET-fusion status of the 17-sample LGFMS comparator arm is inherited from a disease label, with no per-sample fusion call and no citation anywhere in the repository - the exact inference the document forbids in three other places.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript S3.4 '17 LGFMS (FUS::CREB3L2, i.e. another FET fusion)' and S3.0 point 1 'its comparator arm is FUS::CREB3L2-rearranged, i.e. another FET fusion, which is the contrast this part most wants'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'].sample_annotations_verbatim carries no fusion field for GSM600940-GSM600956; every row reads 'Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma N | soft tissue | sample type: tumor biopsy | tissue: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma'. The only basis in the repository is a code comment, research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 328 ('LGFMS added 2026-08-05: FUS::CREB3L2 is a FET fusion...'), with FET_COMPARATOR_BUCKETS on line 330. No PMID, in the manuscript or the module. Against this: S2 refuses the EMC label on ACH-001519 for want of a fusion call; S4 says 'FET status from DepMap's own filtered fusion calls, never from disease labels'; S8.3 says 'A label is not a fusion'. The claim is almost certainly true of LGFMS as a class, which is why this is a P1 rather than a blocker - but nothing reads it, and it is load-bearing for 'two different comparator sets - including one made of another FET fusion'.
p1s.fix: Cite the LGFMS/FUS::CREB3L2 frequency, and add the disclosure S4 already makes for its own arms: this arm's FET status is inherited from the disease label, not called per sample. atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> fet_fusion_sarcoma_subtypes._bound already carries the wording ('Presence of a DISEASE whose defining fusion is a FET fusion. It is not a per-sample fusion call') and can be reused.

p1s.summary: S7's provenance sentence is over-scoped: several numbers 'above' it come from three other producing modules and are not in emc-atr-vulnerability.json at all.
p1s.evidence: S7: 'Every number above is produced by emc_atr_vulnerability.py and lives in its JSON artifact; nothing is hand-typed here that the artifact does not carry, and --check re-derives all of it offline.' The headline's structural numbers (type 2 0 of 30, type 1 8 of 30, type 5 11 of 30, EWSR1::ATF1 fraction 0.267) live in emc-fet-idr-census.json -> positive_controls / emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3 and emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> constructs[*].domains_retained_and_lost; the headline's imported group difference (paclitaxel -0.5255 / t -3.076, azd6738 -0.4911, ve-822 -0.4233, olaparib -1.0163, talazoparib -2.0653) lives in fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> atr_inhibitor_sensitivity_gdsc.by_drug.*.welch_line_median_corrected. Every one reproduces exactly - the artifacts are right, the provenance sentence names the wrong one. Correct only under the reading 'every number in parts A-D'.
p1s.fix: Scope it: 'Every number in parts A-D is produced by emc_atr_vulnerability.py...; the structural numbers in the headline come from emc_fet_idr_census.py / emc_fet_construct_designs.py and the imported group difference from fet_ddr_axis_scan.py, each with its own --check.'

p1s.summary: S2.1's superseded expression reading was corrected in the prose and not in the producing module or its artifact, so the artifact a reader is sent to still carries the withdrawn interpretation.
p1s.evidence: S2.1 now reads 'This row corroborates nothing in either direction', with '(Superseded, retained: "...would be expected to read far higher. Weak corroboration only".)'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_a_hemcss_identity.depmap_expression._reading still states 'a floor-level NR4A3 is evidence against the label', and evidence_chain[1] still ends '...would be expected to read far higher in absolute terms. Reported as weak corroboration only.' The prose is correct now; nothing keeps the pair aligned, and S7 tells the reader the artifact is the home of every statement.
p1s.fix: Propagate the correction into emc_atr_vulnerability.py's _reading and evidence_chain strings and regenerate, or carry S8.3's index-confound sentence there so both copies say the same thing.

p1s.summary: §5's new elimusertib sentence asserts the compound is 'absent from GDSC2 8.5', and no committed artifact establishes that. The nearest-looking field, `part_d.gdsc_meta.drugs_with_data`, is the intersection of a hard-coded wanted-list with the release, not the release's drug catalogue — so it corroborates nothing about a drug nobody asked for, while reading exactly as if it did.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin, §5: 'The compound the source advanced is **elimusertib**, absent from GDSC2 8.5 and named nowhere else here'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json -> part_d.gdsc_meta = {'source': 'GDSC2_8.5_27Oct23', 'n_rows': 242036, 'drugs_with_data': ['azd6738','bortezomib','mk-1775','olaparib','paclitaxel','talazoparib','ve-822']}. In emc_atr_vulnerability.py the loop is `for want in ATRI_NAMES + CONTROL_DRUG_NAMES: sub = df[names.str.contains(want...)]`, and `drugs_with_data` is `sorted(resid_by_drug)` — the seven wanted names that matched. The full 242,036-row release WAS read, so the absence is a $0 re-read away, but it is not in the tree. (The other half of the sentence is sound: the figure caption 'Analysis of DepMap Elimusertib sensitivity scores' is verbatim in atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json -> mechanism_fulltext_xml, Figure 6 panel B.)
p1s.fix: Either add the check to the module (record the release's distinct DRUG_NAME set, or a boolean for elimusertib/BAY-1895344) and cite the field, or downgrade the clause to what is held: 'a compound this analysis did not query in GDSC2 8.5, and one no committed artifact here reports a readout for'.

p1s.summary: The two new §2 passages disagree about what §2.2's boundary rests on. §2.1 (new) says it rests on 'the two readouts below rather than on it'; the second of those two readouts (rewritten in the same commit) now says it 'corroborates nothing in either direction' and that the verdict 'rests on Cellosaurus and the filtered fusion caller' — i.e. on one readout plus the very source §2.1 has just discounted. Correcting the blocker above changes which of these is right, so the two must be fixed together.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript at the pin: §2.1 line 244, '...which is why §2.2's boundary rests on the two readouts below rather than on it'; §2 table, NR4A3-transcript row, '**This row corroborates nothing in either direction**, and §2's verdict does not rest on it — it rests on Cellosaurus and the filtered fusion caller.' Both are additions in 2401803d..78d345d3. The under-counting argument that empties the transcript row is sound and is §8.3's ('The index has no fusion entry... a fusion's contribution to an NR4A3 TPM is systematically under-counted'), so the row's own retreat is right; it is §2.1's 'two readouts' that no longer has a referent.
p1s.fix: In §2.1 write what survives: the boundary rests on the Cellosaurus caution — itself resting on a printed per-line observation whose assay is unstated — and on DepMap's filtered fusion caller, which is a reading of absence. Say plainly that the NR4A3 transcript row is not part of it and why. One sentence, and it removes the contradiction.

p1s.summary: The dependency-modality null SS5 names as missing is computable at $0 from the committed inputs cache, and running it SUPPORTS the passing row rather than undermining it. Leaving it unrun leaves the paper's one positive weaker than its own evidence.
p1s.evidence: SS5: 'no dependency-modality null was run. ... The null that would settle it is a pan-essential score: RPL5 (-2.744) or PLK1 (-2.715), both already computed in part C's per-gene block, and correlated against these drugs nowhere.' Both are in emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_c.gene_effect_by_line (1,178 lines each), and the drug residuals are in #part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug. Spearman on the same line intersections the module uses (my code reproduces every published rho and n exactly - e.g. dependency/azd6738 +0.2520 n=597, ATM-expression/ve-822 -0.1583 n=656): RPL5 azd6738 +0.0370 / ve-822 +0.0365, mean +0.037; PLK1 -0.0109 / +0.0260, mean +0.008; ATM gene effect (near-neutral control) +0.0448 / +0.0450, mean +0.045. Applying the paper's own four bars, none reaches |rho| >= 0.15, none is atri_specific, none beats 0.1968. So 'a strong dependency score of any kind predicts a drug-specific residual' is refuted on the committed data.
p1s.fix: Run the two correlations in the module (they need no fetch), print them beside the passing row, and change 'correlated against these drugs nowhere' to the result: a pan-essential dependency score does not predict the ATR-inhibitor residual (RPL5 rho +0.037, PLK1 +0.008, against +0.212 for the ATR axis), so the passing test is not explained by dependency-score magnitude.

p1s.summary: The passing row is described as agreement 'at MODULE level rather than at target level' and as 'two instruments agreeing about the same three-gene module, not about ATR', but the per-gene decomposition of the composite - from the same committed cache - shows the correlation is carried by ATR and its obligate partner ATRIP, with CHEK1 contributing essentially nothing.
p1s.evidence: Headline line 99 area and SS5. Spearman of each single-gene CRISPR effect against the same drug residuals, from emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_c.gene_effect_by_line and #part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug, on the same n = 597 / 565 line sets: ATR alone rho +0.290 / +0.204 (mean +0.247); ATRIP alone +0.304 / +0.220 (mean +0.262); CHEK1 alone +0.043 / +0.015 (mean +0.029); the three-gene composite +0.252 / +0.173 (mean +0.212); WEE1 alone +0.095 / +0.098 (mean +0.097). The composite is diluted by CHEK1, not carried by it, so the two instruments are agreeing about ATR/ATRIP, not about the module.
p1s.fix: Print the per-gene decomposition and replace the module-level framing with what it shows: the CRISPR-vs-drug agreement is carried by ATR (+0.247) and ATRIP (+0.262) and not by CHEK1 (+0.029). Keep the separate and still-correct point that this says nothing about EMC and that no bar here separates ATR from a neighbouring target on the DRUG side.

p1s.summary: The 2,500-column random background is the normaliser for EVERY expression predictor in part D, not just for the held-out FET signature, and the paper attributes the subspace limitation only to the signature. SS5 also describes the load-bearing ATM predictor as a raw log2(TPM+1) mean, which is not what the module computes.
p1s.evidence: Paper line 736-739 raises the subspace limit for the signature alone ('The paper reproduced the circularity half of that design note and dropped this half'), and SS5 defines the ATM row as 'a log2(TPM+1) mean over the Reactome double-strand-break-response set'. The module at the pin, D2: line 2702 `bg_cols = rng.sample(others, min(2500, len(others)))`; then `mu = bg.mean(axis=1)`, `sd = bg.std(axis=1)`; then for every concept line 2714 `s = (df[cols].mean(axis=1) - mu) / sd`. The artifact records emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.expression_scores_meta.n_background_columns_for_centering: 2500 against #expression_file_choice.n_total_columns_in_file: 19193. So expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair (the load-bearing row) and expr::proliferation_MYC (the control the passing row is measured against) are per-line z-scores against a seeded random 2,500-gene sample of a 19,193-gene matrix, not raw set means.
p1s.fix: State the construction once where the predictors are defined - each expression predictor is the concept mean minus the line's own mean over a seeded random 2,500-gene background, divided by its SD over the same background - and extend the 'not transcriptome-wide' caveat from the signature to all expr:: rows. Correct 'a log2(TPM+1) mean over the Reactome double-strand-break-response set' to the standardised form.

note: Round 5, five blind seats — arithmetic, citations, hostile, regression, statistics — the first round to field the regression lens paper-hardening §4 calls non-optional past round 2. All five verdicts supported_with_reservations: the central claim survived every lens. 13 blocker entries, 13 P1s. FOUR of five seats independently filed the same §2.1 blocker: the paper mis-describes PMID 34413129, saying it states no per-line fusion result when its Figure 2A legend reports one verbatim. Root-caused by the arithmetic seat to emc-systems-map.json objects[18].read_by[97], a round-4 seat entry whose central factual claim is refuted by hemcss-label-priorart.json; that entry is corrected in this commit and the paper is not, because the paper is pinned under this round. The error UNDERSTATES the paper's own evidence, so the repair strengthens §2. NOT converged: blockers are open.
